title: Keep the direction of the CRT implication
place: Final CRT diagram and preceding lemma
body: Scan108 makes surjectivity and bijectivity of the CRT map equivalent to comaximality, and then writes only “\(Q+Q'=A\Rightarrow QQ'=Q\cap Q'\).” Hua's subsection replaces the last implication by an equivalence, which is false: in \(k[x,y]\), \((x)\cap(y)=(xy)\) although \((x)+(y)\ne k[x,y]\). This counterexample concerns the modernized formulation, while the frozen source's CRT chain passes the independent check below.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Polynômes unitaires et idéaux étrangers”, within “Un feuillet d'EGA IV, et de l'algèbre commutative (pages 105 à 110)”; Hua p.107 → scan108. No outside-page conclusion used.
reason: Complete CRT proof and explicit ideals (x),(y) in k[x,y] establish the exact direction; no novelty claim.

title: Connectedness is a substantive insertion in the monic-factor claim
place: Inserted oval at monic-factor hypothesis; unfinished proof below
source_words: Deleted « A local » replaced by « A connexe »; « polynômes unitaires »
body: Scan110 replaces “\(A\) local” by “\(A\) connexe” in the assertion that comaximal ideal factors of a monic principal ideal arise uniquely from monic polynomial factors, but Hua's formulation omits connectedness. That omission changes the assertion: for \(A=k\times k\), the comaximal ideals \(k[T]\times(T)\) and \((T)\times k[T]\) have product \((T,T)\), yet neither has a monic generator. For connected \(A\), the claim admits the independent proof below through the characteristic polynomials of multiplication by \(T\) on the two projective quotient summands.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Polynômes unitaires et idéaux étrangers”; Hua p.109 → scan110. The context statement omits connectedness.
reason: The disconnected example is explicit, and the connected-base theorem is independently proved by characteristic polynomials on constant-rank projective summands.

title: The monic-factor proof stops before the completion argument is stated
place: Last lines of scan110 and completion notation on scan111
source_words: « petite vérification… »; « on voit que c'est vrai sur les »
body: Scan110 flags a “petite vérification” and ends its existence argument at “on voit que c'est vrai sur les.” Hua, “Polynômes unitaires et idéaux étrangers,” describes an existence argument on the completion, but the frozen continuation at scan111 gives only local-ring/completion notation and sketches. The characteristic-polynomial proof supplied in L02 is an independent completion of the argument, not a reading of missing words.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Polynômes unitaires et idéaux étrangers”; Hua pp.109–110 → scans110–111. No completed proof is supplied by the frozen continuation.

title: Preserve the field-extension reading in the proposed criterion
source_words: « une ext. alg. close de k »; « alg. clos »
body: In scan133(v), the frozen reading uses “alg. close” and “alg. clos,” whereas Hua, “Un critère de représentabilité,” states invariance under algebraic separable extensions and flags uncertainty in its own footnote. These conditions are mathematically different: the finite étale functor represented by \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C\) over \(\mathbb R\) has no \(\mathbb R\)-point and two \(\mathbb C\)-points, while its points are unchanged by extensions between algebraically closed fields. This checks the difference between conditions; it does **not** refute Hua's implication under its stronger hypothesis or settle the doubtful source reading.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Un critère de représentabilité”, within “Les « feuilles anciennes » : représentabilité et recollement (pages 130 à 134)”; Hua p.132 → scan133, especially its condition(v) and footnote.

title: The criterion is a proposed result with an unfinished proof
place: Conditions (i)–(v), conclusion, and unfinished local proof
source_words: Inserted « et localisation »; « alors F représentable »; « ils correspondent à des »
body: Scan133 proposes representability by an étale separated quasi-finite object from limit compatibility, faithfully flat descent plus the inserted localization condition, complete-local invariance, separation, and fieldwise finiteness. Its proof begins over a complete local base with algebraically closed residue field, lifts the special-fibre elements uniquely, and breaks off at “ils correspondent à des.” Hua records the unfinished proof, but neither that account nor the elementary checks in this support record supplies a proof of the full criterion.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Un critère de représentabilité”; Hua p.132 → scan133. Full criterion not independently proved here.
relation: restates, with field-condition difference separately recorded

title: The gluing statement includes neighborhood compatibility
place: Inserted neighborhood hypothesis, Cartesian transition square, and conclusion
source_words: « On suppose que pour tt s »; « sur un voisinage ouvert U »
body: Scan135 inserts a hypothesis that each \(X(s)\) has an open-neighborhood model equipped with compatible maps to all the other local objects, in addition to Cartesian specialization maps and their cocycle. Hua's “Le lemme de recollement” omits that hypothesis and treats neighborhood realization as a proof strategy. The weaker context formulation is false even on \(\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb Q}\): the local objects in Check P4 below have compatible Cartesian restrictions but would force an étale morphism to have a non-open image.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Le lemme de recollement”, within “Les « feuilles anciennes » : représentabilité et recollement”; Hua p.134 → scan135. Counterexample targets the context formulation without the insertion.
relation: differs; weakened context existence claim contradicted
reason: Explicit Cartesian specialization data on Spec Q[t] would force a non-open image of an étale morphism; the source with its insertion is not refuted or re-proved.

title: The relative torsor problem is narrower than the general finite-group question
place: Definition of F_G, automorphism note, finite-case question, representability question
source_words: Inserted « étale »; « G commutatif »; uncertain « Cas fini?? »
body: Scan131 asks about the relative pointed-torsor functor for **finite étale** \(G\), under proper flat \(f\) and universal \(f_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_S\), and adds the commutative aside and uncertain “Cas fini??” after the automorphism observation. Hua's “Le foncteur des fibrés pointés” captures the main question but omits those scope markers and the source's quasi-finite qualification “[cas à fibres finies].” The general finite-group case remains a question in this frozen passage; the findings-register item about strict pro-representability in the group variable does not itself answer this different relative question.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Le foncteur des fibrés pointés”; Hua p.130 → scan131. Related “La pro-représentabilité” is in Hua pp.124–126 → scans125–127; those source pages were outside this agent's assigned source-reading subset. Findings-register comparison is thematic, not a proof.
relation: adds scope markers and differs at uncertain final sentence

title: Three diagonalizable-group typescript sheets are absent from the modern account
source_words: « Corollaire 3.2 »; « avec H de type fini sur S »; « Fibrés principaux homogènes sous un groupe diagonalisable »
body: The inverted typescript faces at scans095,097,099 carry a coherent separate sequence, Corollaries 3.2–3.5 on diagonalizable groups followed by §4 on their principal homogeneous spaces, which Hua's modern file does not discuss. In particular scan097 inserts “avec \(H\) de type fini sur \(S\)” and later “qui implique \(N\) de type fini” in the local-diagonalization argument, so this hypothesis belongs to the recorded revision history. These sheets support the package's SGA3 connection independently of the interleaved tame-fundamental-group notes; their presence alone does not date or identify the reused typescript.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: no matching subsection; Hua pp.94,96,98 → scans095,097,099. Adjacent sections are “Le cas où la classe s'annule : Picard formel (pages 91 et 93)” and “Le théorème, et deux exemples (pages 95 et 97)”, followed by “Abhyankar semi-global, et la même classe une deuxième fois (pages 99 et 100)”. Earlier pp.91/93 are outside this package. No whole-file diagonalis hit.

title: The Bourbaki typescript is a separate documentary strand
place: Separate inverted typescript, title through unfinished final sentence
source_words: « Ad majorem fonctori gloriam »; « J'apprends que Grothendieck n'est plus membre de Bourbaki »
body: Scan109 preserves the separate typescript “Ad majorem fonctori gloriam,” responding to Grothendieck's departure from Bourbaki and proposing adoption of his work on categories. Hua's account passes over this sheet while treating the neighboring algebra, and the frozen fragment stops as it introduces “une liste de questions catégoriques.” Neither a named author nor an explicit date is supplied by this frozen passage; “Bourbaki 1960” and “1936” are comparisons within the argument, not a signed dating line.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: no matching subsection; Hua p.108 → scan109 lies in the page span of “Un feuillet d'EGA IV, et de l'algèbre commutative (pages 105 à 110)”. No whole-file Ad majorem/Bourbaki/Kaplanski hits.

title: The English rational-structure sheet interrupts the “feuilles anciennes”
place: English typescript I-6; rational structures and start of §5
source_words: « I-6 »; « 5. Conjugates »; « its graph Γ is a subspace … rational over k »
body: Scan132 is an inverted English typescript page “I-6,” proving preservation of rational subspaces under images and inverse images, the graph criterion for a rational linear map, and beginning “5. Conjugates.” It is not a continuation of the representability argument in the adjoining handwritten pages, and Hua's subsection spanning pp.130–134 does not discuss it. A source, author, or date for that English text remains a reading question; none is inferred here.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: no matching subsection; Hua p.131 → scan132, inside “Les « feuilles anciennes » : représentabilité et recollement (pages 130 à 134)”. No whole-file Conjugates/k-structure/multilinear/rational over hits.

title: The EGA warning is covered, but its local wording should remain exact
source_words: « Attention à l'ambiguïté dans lisse ! »; « noethérien » replaced by « de type fini »
body: Scan106 supplies a substantial EGA IV typescript face, with (17.4.10), the four conditions of (17.5.1), the replacement “localement noethérien” by “localement de type fini,” and the warning about ambiguity in “lisse.” Hua covers this sheet and links the warning to “simple” in its earlier Picard discussion, but the warning on the frozen page does not itself specify that alternative term. The local correction and warning may be cited; the cross-sheet terminological explanation should be credited to Hua and kept distinct from the diplomatic wording.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “« Attention à l'ambiguïté dans lisse ! »”; Hua p.105 → scan106. Its cross-reference to “Pic birationnel” / “Les deux corollaires et la question”, Hua p.74 → scan075, is outside the package; no direct source reading there by this agent.
relation: restates; contextual explanation distinguished from source wording

title: Do not convert sparse completion sketches and headings into propositions
place: Sparse completion sketches, SGA7 heading, cancelled typescript fragment
source_words: « A anneau local » with « intègre » deleted; « son complété »; « Notes pour SGA 7 »; cancelled « (2.1.14.6) »
body: Scan111 gives completion notation and drawings with “intègre” deleted from the local-ring assumption, but no complete proposition or proof; scans112 and118 contribute respectively the heading “Notes pour SGA 7” and a cancelled formula fragment. These are sparse but distinct documentary elements not individually accounted for in Hua's mathematical exposition. Their proximity does not justify completing scan110's unfinished proof or treating the cancelled fragment as part of the inertia argument.

title: The quoted doubt in Hua is not the frozen reading of scan135
place: Uncertain final paragraph and induction plan
source_words: Uncertain « Je vais pour du moins ramener au local »
body: Hua's “Le lemme de recollement” quotes “Je ne suis pas [sûr] de mon raisonnement,” whereas the frozen scan135 ends with the uncertain reading “Je vais pour du moins ramener au local” followed by a noetherian-induction plan. Since no independent image reading is permitted in this research pass, that discrepancy remains a reading question and cannot be promoted into a source quotation or a source-authored self-flag. It has no effect on the independent counterexample to Hua's omitted hypothesis.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Le lemme de recollement”; Hua p.134 → scan135. Hua's quoted admission of uncertainty is not the frozen reading; no image access was used to resolve it.

title: Relative representability and finiteness in families
place: Quasi-finite qualification of the relative representability question
source_words: « quasi-fini sur S [cas à fibres finies] »
body: Scan131's “quasi-fini sur \(S\) [cas à fibres finies]” places its pointed-torsor question beside the constructibility agenda that Hua calls “Finitude en famille” (Hua p.44; related explicit link in “Le foncteur des fibrés pointés,” p.130 = scan131). The shared object is the variation of finite torsor data with the base, but a constructibility program is not the missing representability proof.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex: “Finitude en famille”, Hua p.44 → scan045, outside the package; explicit contextual link also in “Le foncteur des fibrés pointés”, Hua p.130 → scan131. Outside source page not inspected.

title: The universal global-function hypothesis has a separate Picard use
source_words: f_* O_X = O_S, underlined uncertain « universellt|universelle »
body: Scan131 explicitly underlines the universal form of \(f_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_S\), while Hua, “Pic birationnel” / “Le théorème” (Hua p.70), uses the same condition in its discussion of injectivity on Picard functors. That is a useful same-object cross-reference, not a transfer of the birational argument's hypotheses or conclusion to the pointed-torsor problem.
